meta.title: Verified after-tax rule set used by the private calculator
meta.purpose: Encodes ONLY rules that were read from an official IRS or California Franchise Tax Board publication in this session. Anything not verified is absent, and the calculator refuses to guess.
meta.verification_note: Every bracket below is traceable to an S-source in data/findings.json. If a rule is not in this file, the calculator does not apply it and the UI says so. Re-verified line by line on 2026-11-26 against Rev. Proc. 2025-32, IRS Topics 409/559, Pubs 537/544 and the FTB 2025 Form 540 schedules and instructions. A superseded duplicate block that still described the 1% surcharge as unverified was removed, since the same tax is verified and applied under behavioral_health_services_tax.

long_term_capital_gain_2026.note: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.03. The 0% band and the 15% band ceilings are given; above the 15% ceiling the rate is 20%.

federal.like_kind_note: Real property only, held for business or investment; defers rather than eliminates gain.

excluded.reason: Not verified against an official publication in this session. Excluding it may overstate tax on ordinary income.
Rules are date-dependent and were not verified here. Not applied.

excluded.item: Depreciation recapture under section 1250 beyond the 25% unrecaptured ceiling
excluded.reason: Only the maximum 25% unrecaptured rate was verified (S18). Additional depreciation may be recaptured as ordinary income under other rules that were not verified.

depreciation_recapture.rule: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at a MAXIMUM rate of 25%. That 25% is a ceiling, not a flat rate: the gain is added to the taxpayer's other income and taxed at the lesser of the ordinary marginal rate and 25%.
depreciation_recapture.implementation: The calculator takes the recaptured amount, adds it to the taxpayer's other taxable income, and applies min(ordinary marginal rate, 25%) to it.
depreciation_recapture.limitation: Depreciation allowed or allowable in years before 1981 or under straight-line methods can recapture at ordinary rates as section 1245/1250 ordinary income, and additional depreciation beyond straight-line can be recaptured as ordinary income above the 25% ceiling. Those rules were not verified here, so the calculator treats the whole recaptured amount under the 25% ceiling and says so.

california.note: 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules, Form 540. These are the latest schedules published by the FTB at the time of this build. There is NO preferential long-term capital gains rate in California — gain is taxed as ordinary income.

excluded.item: Property tax reassessment on sale (base-year value reset)
excluded.reason: Assessor sources were unreachable. This is a cost to the buyer and therefore affects achievable price, but it is not modelled.
Requires Schedule P (540) preference items from the owner's full return. Thresholds are published so a CPA can be asked.

standard_deduction_2025.note: FTB 2025 Form 540 instructions, 'California Standard Deduction Chart for Most People' (Line 18).

behavioral_health_services_tax.basis: Taxable income on Form 540 line 19 in excess of $1,000,000
behavioral_health_services_tax.note: FTB 2025 Form 540 instructions, Line 62. This is the 1% surcharge commonly called the Mental Health Services Tax.

alternative_minimum_tax.reason_not_applied: The AMT computation requires preference items (Schedule P (540)) that depend on the owner's full return. The threshold is shown so the reader knows when to ask a CPA.

credit_limitation_thresholds_2025.note: FTB 2025 Form 540 instructions, line 32 'AGI Limitation Worksheet'. If federal AGI (Form 540 line 13) exceeds these amounts for the filing status, exemption credits are reduced by $6 for each $2,500 of excess.
credit_limitation_thresholds_2025.corrected: 2026-11-26 — the previous record carried 347,808 / 463,745 / 231,868, which do not appear on the published FTB page. The values above are transcribed from the line 32 table.

disclaimer: This calculator applies published brackets to numbers YOU supply. It is arithmetic, not tax advice. It deliberately omits rules that could not be verified, and it tells you which ones. Every input you type stays in this browser tab: the page has no network calls, no analytics and no storage. Nothing you enter is transmitted, logged or saved.
